Horizon Europe project | University of Trento\
2024 - 2025

## Overview

SUNRISE - Safety Assurance Framework for Connected and Automated Mobility
Systems - is a Horizon Europe project (Grant 101069573) coordinated by
Applus IDIADA, with a 25+ partner consortium spanning automotive suppliers
(Continental, Infineon, Renault, Toyota), research institutions (Chalmers,
University of Warwick), testing organizations (RISE, AVL), and
infrastructure bodies (ERTICO, TNO). It builds a harmonized, scalable
safety assurance framework for CCAM: generating scenarios from an
Operational Design Domain (ODD), allocating them across simulation,
X-in-the-loop, and proving grounds, and aggregating microscopic test
results into macroscopic safety conclusions, with a federated European
scenario data framework, test case library, and handbook as deliverables.

## What I worked on

Our contribution is a data-driven framework for quantifiable safety
assessment: a stochastic model that predicts safety outcomes (collision,
near-miss, safe) for any parametrized driving scenario, with quantified
uncertainty, using bootstrap aggregation - an ensemble of compact
feed-forward neural networks, each trained on a random sample of the
scenario space. Unlike running full simulations, the trained ensemble
executes in microseconds, enabling both offline diagnosis and online,
real-time decision support.

I applied the framework to MPTree - the planner developed in my PhD - for
a full safety assessment and a real-time safe speed recommendation, and to
CoDriver's larger simulation dataset for failure mode identification,
showing the framework transfers across planning agents without
modification. I also developed the two self-driving agents used as
systems under test throughout this work: the Intelligent Driver Model
(IDM) baseline and MPTree/Motion Planner itself.

## Applications

- **Safety assessment** - estimating collision probability over
  hypothetical risk subdomains (e.g. a distracted driver missing the
  merge, at various relative speeds and maneuver aggressiveness) via
  fast Monte Carlo evaluation of the trained ensemble.
- **Failure mode identification** - sampling near the learned
  collision boundary, clustering the resulting near-miss trajectories,
  and replaying a handful of representative cases per cluster to
  diagnose specific weaknesses instead of reviewing logs by hand.
- **Safe speed advisor** - an online application that, given the
  current traffic state, scans candidate ego velocities and recommends
  the one minimizing collision risk in real time.

## Publication

*Bootstrapped Neural Models for Predicting Self-Driving Vehicle
Collisions With Quantified Confidence: Offline and Online Applications*
(A. Cherubini, G. P. Rosati Papini, A. Plebe, **M. Piazza**, M. Da Lio -
IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles, 2024), and a chapter of my PhD
thesis.
